question: The two fundamental properties that make fingerprints reliable evidence for personal identification are permanence (patterns do not change from foetal development to decomposition) and uniqueness (no two individuals share identical ridge patterns).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Fingerprint identification rests on exactly these two properties: permanence (ridge patterns are established in utero and persist until decomposition) and uniqueness (no two individuals, including identical twins, share identical fingerprint patterns at the level of minutiae detail).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Friction ridge skin forms its characteristic patterns during foetal development (approximately 10–17 weeks) and these patterns persist unchanged until decomposition after death. Combined with the statistical uniqueness of each individual's ridge detail, these two properties form the scientific basis of dactylography as a method of identification.
